scope: Four task addenda only; original 31 imported assignments are frozen and unreviewed.

tasks.evidenceReview: The original APP-01 assignment creates the application shell and generic navigation placeholders. The approved November 16 specification Section 16.4 supplies exactly three tab labels and nine grouping labels. The addendum keeps APP-01 as the prerequisite root and leaves the 24 menu destinations/defaults to the later view assignment. No existing live tenant menu or verified metadata ID is asserted.
tasks.languageReview: I read the objective, expanded scope, twelve tab/group rows, two build steps, readiness text, role explanation and result checks. They state the user-visible tab/group result directly, preserve the supplied business labels, and distinguish shell creation from later bindings without requiring the assignee to interpret numbered requirements.
tasks.meaningReview: I reconciled the exact ordered tab labels, the two/three/four group counts and all nine header spellings with the approved specification. APP-01 remains an Associate Consultant assignment reviewed by a Senior Consultant, has no predecessor, creates no extra contribution tab, and receives no dependency on reports or security work that would create a cycle.

tasks.evidenceReview: The original CFG-03 assignment owns catalogue forms, inherited fields, active filtering, audit and basic permissions. The updated specification Sections 7 and 16.1 explicitly replaces the blanket maintenance grant with three business and ten technical catalogues. I checked all thirteen names, the inherited Code/Name/Active?/Sort contract, Description on KPI Aggregation Method, and Frequency on Scorecard Cadence. The increment object/form is an earlier scheduling-amendment output, so only its privilege assignment waits for that target.
tasks.languageReview: I read every catalogue row and each field-editability row without source references. Each identifies a concrete catalogue or field and names the allowed users, with lookup access explained separately. The task preserves the original catalogue setup scope and describes missing Group/target/capability information locally rather than turning it into a discovery assignment.
tasks.meaningReview: I reconciled maintenance for Supplier Commodity, NAICS Classification and KPI Category to the application-admin group or Administrators, and all ten technical domains to Administrators only. The new grant applies across direct and administrative paths while Code first-use stability, used-Cadence Frequency immutability, inactive historical references, inherited field ownership, audit and inverse suppression remain as before. No field, Code, seed or inheritance change is assigned.

tasks.evidenceReview: The original SEC-26 task owns nuanced application/object/record/workflow security. The approved specification fixes the three tab audiences and reviewer-only menu, while retaining supplier scope and existing action controls. I checked that this addendum supplies policies rather than trying to bind menu records before the later reporting task creates them. Catalogue record/field maintenance is owned by CFG-03, avoiding duplicated configuration ownership.
tasks.languageReview: I read the original retained security scope, added audience policies, current-review condition, local waiting information and acceptance examples. The task explains who receives each tab and why tab membership cannot grant operations. Native Group bindings remain supplied configuration inputs; no system-processing grant or invented principal is assigned.
tasks.meaningReview: Supplier Scorecards remains internal and scoped. Program Administration allows the application-admin group and Administrators; Program Development permits Administrators only. Review eligibility is for the applicable cycle and is passed to final menu assembly. Existing form/workflow/publication predecessors remain; no dependence on later RPT-27 menu records or grant of contribution/override/publication actions through tab access was introduced.

tasks.evidenceReview: The updated specification Section 16.4 supplies all 24 menu labels, nine tab/group placements, destination objects/views and three default views. I compared each rendered row with that table and the approved conversation. The retained RPT-27 scope already owns native views and reporting. KPI and Program form prerequisites are added because final navigation opens those experiences. Only unverified native binding support is an input; newly created identifiers are build outputs.
tasks.languageReview: I read all 27 feature rows, three ordered instructions, result checks, predecessor outputs and task-local waiting statements. Each menu path names the tab, grouping and displayed item before stating what opens. Blank defaults, reviewer-only visibility and the increment-specific blocker are understandable without source references, and the original reporting/ranking responsibilities remain explicit.
tasks.meaningReview: I reconciled the five/nine/ten menu counts, exact destinations and item order. Defaults remain Scorecard Overview, blank, blank. Final assembly consumes rather than redefines the security policies and catalogue privileges. No My Contribution Tasks menu, fourth tab, abstract-catalogue form, or unrestricted Generation Delay creation path is added. Native audit, immutable Versions and existing contribution links remain in use; the separate increment object/form is not created here.
